solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Exhausted couple apt to collapse, needing day in

indicators.note: the day abbreviation is placed inside the rearranged letters
letters that collapse fall apart and are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A worn-out pair seem likely to drop unless they get a day's rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exhausted' could suit the couple, but it is the definition; 'needing' is a link, and the rearranged letters before the D goes in are CLAPPEOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Clapped-out is British slang for worn out or exhausted, used of people or machines.

clue.text: Around the end of tour driver becomes cross

indicators.note: one word goes around the other, here the driver surrounds a letter

parts.note: a cabby is a taxi driver

indicators.note: signals the last letter of the word tour

explanation.surface: A driver gets grumpy by the end of a tour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the end of' takes R from tour, and 'Around' puts CABBY round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Crabby and cross are synonyms for bad-tempered or irritable.

clue.text: Property? Ton may be carried by donkeys

indicators.note: something carried by donkeys sits inside them, signalling a container

parts.note: asses are donkeys

explanation.surface: A heavy load could be borne by a team of donkeys as property.
explanation.definitionFit: Assets are things owned, a person's or company's property and resources.

clue.text: They may come in in the middle of a sentence

definitions.text: They may come in in the middle of a sentence

parts.words: They may come in in the middle of a sentence
parts.note: reads like grammar about words in a sentence, but the sentence is a prison term and these people call on inmates while it is being served

explanation.surface: A grammatical observation about words that interrupt a sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Visitors to a jail arrive while a prisoner is partway through serving a sentence.

clue.text: The night rider's friend is someone of unknown potential

parts.note: night is dark
a horse is the companion of a rider

explanation.surface: A highwayman's horse becomes a mysterious figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark horse is an idiom for a competitor or person whose abilities are little known.

clue.text: Brown bits and pieces left to go out

indicators.note: the left abbreviation goes out, so it is removed from the word

parts.note: lumber is junk, odds and ends of household clutter

explanation.surface: Brown fragments are abandoned outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go out' removes L (left) from LUMBER.
explanation.definitionFit: Umber is a natural brown earth pigment and the colour named after it.

clue.text: Bill having got posh is prohibited

parts.note: a tab is a bill or account at a bar
U means upper-class, posh in British usage

explanation.surface: An expensive restaurant bill is not allowed.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabu is a variant spelling of taboo, forbidden by custom.

clue.text: Article I had to keep partner excited

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: one piece keeps another inside it, signalling a container

parts.note: I'd is a contraction of I had
a mate is a partner

explanation.surface: A thing I possessed held my companion in a state of excitement.
explanation.definitionFit: Animated means lively and spirited, close in sense to excited.

clue.text: Insecure Sudan yet to reform

indicators.note: reforming reshapes the letters into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A political comment on a fragile African state awaiting reform.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsteady means not firm or stable, hence insecure.

clue.text: A well-rounded intellectual or phony ass with a nice manner?

indicators.note: something phony is fake, so the letters are rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: Is a polymath genuine, or merely a fool with charming ways?
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the fodder and gives no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A Renaissance man is a person with wide learning in many fields, a polymath.

clue.text: Musically, very much part of wassailing

indicators.note: the answer is a part of the following word

explanation.surface: Musically speaking, a lot of carol-singing goes on.
explanation.definitionFit: Assai is an Italian musical direction meaning very, as in allegro assai.

clue.text: Be joined by Irish revolutionary in clothes appropriate for crimes

indicators.note: these pieces go inside the word for clothes

parts.note: robes are garments
taken as written

indicators.note: turning round, so the Irish abbreviation is read backwards

explanation.surface: An Irish rebel in suitable dress joins in criminal acts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns IR into RI; BE plus RI go 'in' ROBES.
explanation.definitionFit: Robberies are crimes of theft, a specific example of crimes.

clue.text: Contract to marry little woman includes rubbish

indicators.note: one piece includes the other within it

parts.note: Beth is one of the four March sisters in Little Women
rot is nonsense, rubbish

explanation.surface: An engagement contract to wed a young lady contains nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: Little Women is Louisa May Alcott's novel; Beth March is one of the sisters.
explanation.definitionFit: To betroth is to promise in marriage, a contract to marry.

clue.text: Pub drink could make you stagger and be ill, we hear

indicators.note: signals that the words are spoken and the sound is what counts

parts.note: to reel is to stagger and to ail is to be ill

explanation.surface: A pub drink that leaves you lurching and sick.
explanation.walkthrough: Real ale is a British term for traditionally brewed cask beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Real ale is cask-conditioned beer served in British pubs.

clue.text: The boss's boss will be too hard to understand

definitions.meaning: a superior above one's own immediate manager, someone above in the hierarchy

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means both higher in the chain of command and beyond comprehension.

clue.text: Rod's refusal to take notes (in Biology)

definitions.note: read as rod is, the 's standing for is

parts.note: no is a refusal
a chord is several notes sounded together

explanation.surface: Rod declines to take notes in a biology lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: '(in Biology)' points to the scientific field; 'take' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A notochord is the flexible rod of cells supporting the body in embryonic vertebrates.

clue.text: Find one's way through a den, hurt, dishevelled

indicators.note: messed up and untidy, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone injured and untidy picks a path through a lair.
explanation.definitionFit: To unthread is to find a way through something tangled, as through a maze.

clue.text: In front of the agent I had to be fearless

indicators.note: takes the front letter of the next word

parts.note: a rep is a sales agent or representative
I'd is a contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Getting ahead of the secret agent required courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'front of' takes T from 'the'; 'to be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Intrepid means bold and undaunted, a synonym of fearless.

clue.text: It could be abandoned in Lent season

definitions.text: It could be abandoned in Lent season

indicators.note: abandoned means wild and unrestrained, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something that might be given up during Lent.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a luxury given up for Lent is something you can do without.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dispensable can be given up, as Lenten sacrifices usually are.

clue.text: Territorials taking fight on in old city

parts.note: to spar is to box or fight
TA is the Territorial Army, the British army reserve

explanation.surface: Reservist soldiers take up a fight in an ancient city.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparta was a powerful city-state of ancient Greece.

clue.text: Sculpture visible to all in the country

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a state is a country
U is the British film certificate for universal viewing

explanation.surface: A sculpture on public display somewhere in the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British film classification meaning suitable for all audiences.
explanation.definitionFit: A statue is a sculpted figure, a type of sculpture.

clue.text: Unorthodox believer at this place twitching

parts.note: here means at this place
a tic is an involuntary twitching

explanation.surface: A dissenter twitches nervously here.
explanation.definitionFit: A heretic holds religious beliefs contrary to orthodox doctrine.

clue.text: It's good after study to have a dance

indicators.note: good comes after study in the answer

parts.note: to con is to study or pore over

explanation.surface: After a spell of study it is good to have a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The conga is a Latin American line dance.

clue.text: Certainly no place for a happy hen party

definitions.text: Certainly no place for a happy hen party

parts.words: Certainly no place for a happy hen party
parts.note: reads as a venue unsuited to a bride's celebration, but the hens are birds and the place is an arena where cocks fight

explanation.surface: A venue that would spoil a bachelorette celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockpit was a pit for cockfighting, hardly a happy place for poultry.

clue.text: Language translatable into neat prose

indicators.note: translating changes the form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Tidy writing can be rendered in another tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Esperanto is a constructed international language.

clue.text: Worthiness of home ritual

indicators.note: the answer is drawn out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: The value of a domestic routine.
explanation.definitionFit: Merit is the quality of deserving praise, worth.

clue.text: Comic theologian seen at party

parts.note: a do is a party
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian's degree

explanation.surface: A funny theologian turns up at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: Ken Dodd was a famous British comedian; 'seen at' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ken Dodd was a celebrated comic from Liverpool.

clue.text: A wicket at the end of one's lawn?

definitions.text: A wicket at the end of one's lawn?

parts.words: A wicket at the end of one's lawn?
parts.note: suggests cricket stumps on a lawn, but a wicket is also a small gate, found where a garden ends

explanation.surface: Cricket stumps set up at the bottom of the lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the wicket is the stumps; a wicket is also a small door or gate.
explanation.definitionFit: A small entrance at the edge of a lawn is a gate into the garden.
